raised.quote:
if (!allowedKeys.has(verdict.new_issue_key!)) { skipped++; continue; }
      pushInto(byKey, verdict.new_issue_key!, verdict);
raised.claim: Verdicts can create and attach to a new issue even when their rows contradict its scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: A new issue scoped to `candidates_count > 0` can be created from a verdict for a zero-candidate row; the job then records the issue link for that row, even though the same verdict would be rejected if the issue already existed.

raised.claim: The model-authored issue body can still override or invalidate the generated scope block.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the prose includes a fenced `triage-scope` example before the appended block, the parser takes that first match: a valid example becomes the routing scope, while invalid JSON makes the issue appear unscoped.

raised.claim: The saturation check ignores rows already accepted for the same issue in the current plan.
raised.why_it_breaks: An issue with 11 post-creation rows can accept all five matching verdicts in one run because every check still sees 11, leaving it at 16 instead of the cap of 12.

raised.claim: An empty probe can authorize an absence verdict even when the other probe found the beer.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the brewery-only search returns nothing because the shop uses an alias, but the name-only search returns the actual beer under its canonical brewery, the guard still accepts `not_on_untappd` and the classification blocks the metered fallback.

raised.claim: Adding one enumerated ID makes a class-only `where` legal without narrowing that predicate.
raised.why_it_breaks: A proposal with `beer_ids: [1]` and `where: [review_class = matcher_bug]` passes validation, and because the branches are ORed, it still accepts every future `matcher_bug` verdict regardless of beer ID.

raised.claim: The legality check accepts predicates that mention another column but do not narrow the class.
raised.why_it_breaks: A proposal combining `review_class = matcher_bug` with `candidates_count >= 0` is legal and accepts every matcher-bug row with a normal nonnegative candidate count, recreating a whole-class catch-all.

raised.claim: An existing issue with a syntactically valid but illegal scope can still accept attachments.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an existing issue is edited or backfilled with a structured block containing only `review_class = matcher_bug`, parsing succeeds and any matcher-bug verdict can attach until the saturation guard intervenes; only new proposals go through `isLegalScope`.

raised.quote: return { key: i.key, title: i.title, body: i.body, labels, scope: i.scope, verdicts };
raised.claim: The published cohort can include IDs for which the planner accepted no founding verdict.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a proposal lists beers 1 and 999 but only beer 1 is in the batch and routed to the issue, 999 is still published in the scope; if that beer appears on a later run, its ID alone lets it pass the scope guard even though it was never part of the founding cohort.

raised.claim: Guard counters are not logged when the model returns a verdict for every row.
raised.why_it_breaks: If all 50 rows receive verdicts but all 50 are rejected by the scope guard, `covered` is still 50 and the warning is suppressed; a full batch of degraded absence verdicts likewise emits no guard counts.

raised.claim: The new absence downgrade is reported as `wontfix` even though it is stored as `matcher_bug`.
raised.why_it_breaks: With no probe evidence, a `not_on_untappd` verdict becomes a quiet `matcher_bug`; the job saves that class but increments `wontfix`, so the daily digest says the beer was intentionally excluded even though it remains eligible for enrichment.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: The saturation query compares timestamp strings rather than instants.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a GitHub creation time of `2026-08-14T00:00:00Z`, a review at `2026-08-14T00:00:00.500Z` sorts before the creation string because `.` sorts before `Z`, so it is not counted even though it is later.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: The saturation count forgets attachments when their failure rows are cleared or reopened.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an issue has received 12 post-creation rows and one beer later matches or crosses the zero-candidate boundary, its row is deleted or its `reviewed_at` is reset; the count drops below 12 even though the GitHub issue still carries all 12 examples.

raised.quote:
reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: Reopening a failure leaves its new authoritative issue link in place after clearing the rest of the verdict.
raised.why_it_breaks: A beer attached to #347 that later moves from zero to three candidates has its class, note, and review time cleared, but `issue_number` still says 347; a direct issue-link query reports an active association while the row is awaiting retriage.

raised.claim: The migration uses the first arrow reference in a free-text note rather than identifying the appended issue link.
raised.why_it_breaks: A legacy note such as `old route → #347; alias gap → #405` gets linked to #347 instead of #405, and a quiet note such as `compare → #347` can acquire a link despite never having been attached.

raised.claim: The prompt can hide the scope and does not tell the model which issues are saturated, even though both now determine routing eligibility.
raised.why_it_breaks: For an issue with 2,000 characters of prose before its appended scope, the model sees the matching title and prose but not the scope; it also sees no saturation count, so it can keep choosing an issue that the planner will reject on every run.

raised.claim: The strict tool schema permits scope operators and column combinations that the analysis parser rejects.
raised.why_it_breaks: A term with `col: 'candidates_count'`, `op: 'contains'`, and `value: '0'` satisfies the tool schema but fails `ScopeTermSchema`, so parsing the analysis rejects unrelated valid verdicts in the same response as well.
